# Anti-AI-Slop & Bespoke Design Guidelines

## 1. What is "AI Slop" in Frontend UI?
"AI Slop" in frontend design refers to the repetitive, predictable, and soulless patterns generated by large language models when prompted to create a website or application. Because models are trained on countless generic templates and landing page clones, they produce a statistical average of the web: bland, repetitive, and visually indistinguishable from thousands of other AI-generated pages.

---

## 2. Common AI Clichés vs. Bespoke Solutions

| AI Cliché Pattern | Why It Fails | Bespoke Professional Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| **Gradient Hero Heading** (e.g., Indigo-to-Cyan or Purple-to-Pink gradient text on H1) | Screams "AI generated 2023 tech template". Hard to read on varied displays, lacks editorial maturity. | High-contrast solid typography with deliberate weight, editorial kerning, or contrasting italic/serif accent words. |
| **Endless Rounded Floating Cards** (`rounded-2xl shadow-xl border border-gray-100 bg-white p-6`) | Creates visual clutter, fragments related information, wastes vertical and horizontal real estate. | Border-based structural grids, alternating surface bands, subtle inset dividers, and varied informational hierarchy. |
| **Washed-out Gray Text** (`text-slate-400` on white, or `text-zinc-600` on black) | Violates WCAG accessibility standards, causes severe eye fatigue, renders unreadable on low-brightness screens. | Strict semantic contrast: High-contrast primary text (`text-slate-900` / `#0f172a`), balanced secondary text (`text-slate-600` / `#475569`). |
| **Centered Everything** (Centered badge, centered H1, centered subtitle, centered CTA buttons) | Weak scanning eye path (F-pattern or Z-pattern), feels static and junior. | Dynamic asymmetrical grid, left-aligned structured content paired with rich interactive previews or editorial sidebars. |
| **Overuse of Generic Glows & Blobs** (Giant blurred radial gradients floating behind cards) | Distracting visual noise, masks poor layout foundation, degrades GPU rendering on lower-tier devices. | Clean, intentional lighting: subtle border highlights, purposeful focus states, clean structural shadows. |
| **Identical Button Shapes** (Pill-shaped or heavily rounded buttons with identical weights) | Flattens visual hierarchy, users cannot distinguish primary vs secondary vs destructive actions. | Defined button hierarchy: Solid High-Contrast Primary, Crisp Ghost/Outline Secondary, Minimal Subdued Tertiary/Text button. |

---

## 3. Brand Archetypes & Distinct Aesthetics

Before writing CSS/Tailwind, adopt a clear brand aesthetic tailored to the domain:

### Archetype A: Technical & Industrial (DevTools, Infrastructure, Fintech)
- **Palette:** Monochromatic base (Zinc/Slate), high-contrast safety accent (International Orange, Amber, or Electric Cobalt).
- **Typography:** Crisp geometric grotesque (Geist, Inter, Roboto Mono) with monospaced metadata labels.
- **Borders & Radii:** Sharp or minimal radius (`rounded-sm` or `rounded-md`), crisp `1px` high-contrast borders (`border-zinc-800` or `border-zinc-200`).
- **Data Density:** High density, compact row heights, explicit tabular figures (`tabular-nums`).

### Archetype B: Editorial & Humanist (Education, Publishing, Research)
- **Palette:** Warm parchment or ivory background tones, deep espresso or ink text, muted forest green or terracotta accents.
- **Typography:** Refined serif for headings (Newsreader, Merriweather, Playfair) paired with clean humanist sans for body (Source Sans, Plus Jakarta Sans).
- **Layout:** Generous line height (1.6 - 1.7), controlled measure (65–75 characters per line), elegant column layouts.

### Archetype C: Modern Productive Software (SaaS, Workspaces, CRM)
- **Palette:** Clean slate/neutral backgrounds, single vibrant functional accent (Deep Teal, Indigo, or Violet), distinct semantic state colors (Emerald for success, Rose for danger).
- **Components:** Compact inputs, clear label-to-control relationships, multi-level navigation drawers.
- **Rhythm:** Standard 8px spatial grid with subtle elevation layering.

---

## 4. The 3-Second Visual Litmus Test

Look at the rendered screen and ask:
1. *Could this interface belong to any random fake startup?* If yes, refactor.
2. *Does the page feel alive and functional with real-world edge cases (e.g., 80-character titles, missing user avatars, zero data)?*
3. *Is the visual rhythm driven by intentional typography and spacing, rather than arbitrary decorative boxes?*
